speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have concerns about a skin lesion; please describe its location, size, color, and if you have noticed any changes in shape or bleeding.

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Given your age, smoking history, and the specific description of a non-healing, crusty lesion on the penis and finger, I need to determine if this is a malignancy. Have you noticed any pain, itching, or ulceration in these areas, and how long have these lesions been present?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (penis and finger). The clinical presentation of non-healing, crusty, painless lesions on sun-exposed skin (finger) and the genitalia in a patient with a significant smoking history and prior failed treatments for syphilis is highly suggestive of malignancy. A biopsy of both lesions is required for definitive histopathological confirmation and staging.
